rubric.evidence: models/fashion-clip-search/worker.js runs the REAL CLIPModel (patrickjohncyh/fashion-clip, immutable revision 7e3ba62ce16b379a1ab479346b66f192e76f51b7 — pinned byte-for-byte to main's classification demo): catalog images embedded once via processor → image_embeds; each free-text query embedded via tokenizer → text_embeds; ranking = real cosine similarity of the actual tensors. Retrieval direction verified LIVE on the pre-rebase branch in headless Chrome: 'something with wheels' → #1 bicycle (0.226), 8 ranked cards, 1.7s search, WASM.

embedCatalog() returns {n, dim, ms}; search() returns {ranked:[{idx,score}], ms}. Semantic sanity = sensible ranking for descriptive queries (verified for 'something with wheels'); re-verification pending on this branch.

At-a-glance declares exact source id + immutable revision (linked to the HF tree at that revision), task zero-shot-image-classification (used as text→image retrieval), architecture FashionCLIP 2.0 (CLIP ViT-B/32, 512-d projection), dtype fp32, artifact onnx/model.onnx exactly 605,804,513 bytes (578 MiB), backend WASM, license MIT, web APIs. model-loader entry matches (modelId + revision + dtype fp32 sizeMB 578).

Uses lib/model-loader.js createModelLoader (shared auto-init; Download only when absent; Update/Re-download/Clear per state). Cache key includes the pinned revision (modelId::revision) so the shared transformers-cache serves BOTH the classification demo and this one from a single 578 MiB download. Conformance assertion revision-pin-matches-main-fashion-clip enforces the pins stay identical — a one-sided bump fails the gate.

status line surfaces checking→initialising→ready via the loader, then 'Embedding the catalog…' → 'Ready to search.' → Searching…/Done./Failed with .err styling; worker errors propagate; retry = re-run. Download UX: total size disclosed BEFORE the fetch starts (Download button shows ~578 MB; the resource-warning note discloses exact bytes + memory/mobile caveats pre-fetch) with real per-file progress via the shared loader. Offline/eviction handled by the shared loader.
Query chips (click + keyboard via button semantics), query input, Search button. Native controls; status role=status aria-live; results are cards with img alt text.
Every score is a real cosine similarity computed in the worker from the model's actual embeddings; the ranking order comes from those numbers. Nothing precomputed or canned.

Design-system classes only; native controls; result images carry alt text (catalog labels); live region on status; resource-warning is a role=note. Sub-24px tap targets likely on chips — flagged for the responsive matrix pass.

CLIP_CSS uses an auto-fill grid (minmax 11rem) so cards reflow to one column on narrow screens; query-row wraps; resource-warning wraps. Full 360x740 + 1280x800 matrix with real runs pending. support=needs-review on both classes until then.

All inference runs in the Web Worker; catalog embeddings cached in the worker so queries are a single text pass + cosine sweep (verified 1.7s post-embed). fp32 578 MiB is a heavy first download — honestly disclosed pre-fetch (resource-warning) + mitigated by the shared-cache story (same revision as the classification demo).

summary: Revision-1 critique for fashion-clip-search (patrickjohncyh/fashion-clip at immutable revision 7e3ba62…, zero-shot-image-classification, Transformers.js, WASM fp32, ~578 MiB, MIT). New capability: the retrieval direction of FashionCLIP — free-text query ranks a whole catalog via real cosine similarities; catalog embedded once + cached in the worker. Distinct from the built classification demo (image→labels); shares the same weights + pinned revision so transformers-cache serves both from one download (enforced by a conformance assertion). Honest download UX: exact bytes + memory/mobile caveats disclosed pre-fetch (resource-warning, mirrors main's FashionCLIP pattern). 3 use-case rungs: basics (search the catalog), practical (zero-shot tagging), wild (absurd queries).
